summary.intent: Plan, execute, and ship Phase 72 (SDK write-plane durability/correctness) after auditing pending todos for drift from Phases 70/70.1/71, then diagnosing and fixing CI failures (web-e2e, desktop-e2e, sdk-e2e) that took priority over planning, and finally hardening the whole monorepo's test-file typechecking before shipping.
summary.outcome: Retired 8 stale Phase 71 todos and folded 2 new ones into Phase 72/73 scope; fixed and merged 3 CI regressions (web floor-store helper, FUSE seq-equivocation, sdk-e2e Test 21 flake) via PRs #600/#601, plus 4 additional web-e2e timing flakes found via extensive local repro; planned and executed all 10 Phase 72 plans across 7 waves (all 6 success criteria met, TDD throughout); on top of that, fixed 113 pre-existing test-file TypeScript errors across 5 packages and wired CI to typecheck test files (build-first) per user direction; discovered 36 skipped sdk tests including overdue TODO(phase 63/65) blocks and dispatched an agent to resolve them before final ship — that resolution was still in progress when the transcript ends.

repo: cipher-box's ci-e2e.yml (Web E2E + Desktop E2E) triggers ONLY on push-to-main or workflow_dispatch — never on pull_request — so PR authors must manually dispatch against their branch to get real e2e signal before merging
gh workflow run dispatch requires `--ref <branch>` (not `-f ref=<branch>`) on this repo's older workflow_dispatch definition; `-f ref=` returns HTTP 422 'Unexpected inputs'

Root pnpm typecheck only ran each package's tsconfig.build.json (which excludes tests) — test files were never typechecked in CI despite each package's base tsconfig.json including them; fixed by adding a per-package `typecheck` script (tsc --noEmit) chained after builds

@cipherbox/* cross-package types resolve via workspace symlinks to each package's built dist (no path aliases or TS project references) — a package's test-inclusive typecheck needs upstream deps already built, so typecheck must run build-first, interleaved/after in dependency order

Playwright's ciFloor() helper only raises wait timeouts (e.g. waitForItemToDisappear) to 60s under CI; local runs use the bare 15-30s timeout, causing IPNS-gated operations (deletes, mkdirs, restores) to flake locally even though they pass reliably in CI
playwright.config.ts webServer.reuseExistingServer is `!process.env.CI`, so setting CI=1 locally to get the 60s ciFloor also disables server reuse and fights an already-running local stack

Phase 71 (#599) shipped without retiring its 8 source todos from pending/ (repo convention retires todos by deleting/moving them, not by marking done) — drift can accumulate silently across ship cycles
cargo check for winfsp feature fails on macOS due to windows-future dependency not compiling — known, unrelated to code changes; Windows CI is authoritative for that platform

Repo's raw hook-definition JSON (gsd-core hooks) contains literal control characters inside string values, breaking standard JSON.parse — requires a custom lenient parser that escapes control chars only inside string literals

Phase 62 retired several SDK types (FileMetadata, FolderChild, FolderEntry, FolderMetadata, VaultInit.rootFolderKey) but test files across packages/sdk were never migrated, accumulating alongside an unrelated vitest v2→v3 Mock-generics break

code.finding: publish_file_node hardcoded seq=1 on first-publish gated only by 'inode cid empty', so a stale/replayed UploadComplete re-seals at seq=1 with a new CID and trips Phase 71's anti-equivocation gate; fixed by resolving IPNS state first and routing Found-but-changed cases into the existing CAS bump path instead of skipping

publish_with_cas_retry gained an optional preresolved_seq param so callers that already resolved the sequence (e.g. content_ops.rs Found path) skip a redundant second resolve; conflict-retry path always re-resolves since pre-resolved values go stale after a conflict

Test driver used pre-#599 share DTO field names (readDescriptorRef, rootIpnsName) in the /shares POST body and received-share reads, causing 400s from forbidNonWhitelisted validation after the FUSE fix; renamed to encryptedReadKey/shareRootIpnsName

readDurableFloors/writeDurableSeqFloor still read the old generation-high-water/seq-high-water IndexedDB stores retired by Phase 70.1's collapse into a single rotation-floor store (DB v2, keyed by nodeId) — helper silently returned undefined

getWriteBodyParams (and its bin/index.ts twin) fail-open on a transient IPNS resolve miss when a real writeKey is present, silently sealing an empty write chain; fixed to throw naming the folder's ipnsName, while preserving the legitimate zero-writeKey read-only fallback

Test 21 (D-06) asserted exactly one-200/one-409 for concurrent same-CID first-publish, but Phase 71's idempotency guarantee makes two-200s a valid outcome too — rewritten to accept both shapes while still rejecting any non-409 rejection

A skipped block asserting params.folderKey on updateFileMetadata was retired-premise (moveItem no longer re-encrypts, per-file Node model); type-reconciled by mapping to fileWriteKey with a comment since the block is skip'd and never executes — flagged as needing a real phase-65 rewrite

workflow: When a local e2e re-run repeatedly flakes on a different test each time, check whether the harness applies CI-only timeout floors (like ciFloor) before assuming ambient stack degradation — running under the CI timeout regime locally (even via a temporary config patch, reverted after) is the representative way to verify fixes without burning CI minutes
Sequencing a large cross-cutting hardening task (fixing test-type drift + CI wiring) as the LAST plan in a phase avoids redoing the fix after every subsequent plan adds new test files

Dispatching two disjoint-package fixer agents in parallel for a large TS-drift cleanup, each verifying zero as-any/@ts-ignore hacks and full test-suite parity, scaled well for mechanical-but-careful migration work

For unattended unattended execution across many serialized-on-one-file plans, running plans sequentially on the main tree (skipping worktree isolation) sidesteps pnpm-monorepo node_modules-in-worktree failures when parallelism wouldn't help anyway

User course-corrected twice on the typecheck-ordering question (test-before-build → build-before-test) once shown the actual dist-based type resolution constraint — worth confirming technical constraints before committing to an ordering, since the 'ideal' order can be infeasible

friction: Repeated local Playwright runs (5+ full-workflow passes, ~10-20 min each) were needed to get past a chain of unrelated local-only timing flakes (4.10, 4.11, 2.1) before reaching the actual target tests (6.6.2, 8.2) — the local/CI timeout asymmetry (ciFloor) made 'verify locally' unexpectedly expensive and required a temporary playwright.config.ts patch to truly mirror CI
gh workflow run dispatch failed with HTTP 422 using the documented -f ref= syntax; had to discover --ref works instead
Hook definition JSON files contain raw control characters that break standard JSON parsing, requiring a hand-written lenient parser mid-session
Git commit appeared to hang/time out due to 1Password SSH-signing prompt on lint-staged (~2 min), requiring manual verification that the commit actually landed rather than retrying blindly
A cat-file-based check of commit contents produced a false negative disagreement with `git status`, costing an extra investigation round before trusting the decisive check
Directory confusion early on (checked resolved/ instead of completed/) required a user correction mid-turn to find the retired-todo evidence
CI-only e2e workflows don't run on PRs, so validating fixes pre-merge required manual workflow_dispatch against each fix branch rather than relying on standard PR checks
